why: Gets legs warm and loose before any ball work.
say: Go to the half-court line and back, a new movement each trip.
how: Players form 3–4 lines on the baseline.
First player in each line goes to half court, jogs back on the sideline.
Movements: jog, high knees, butt kickers, shuffles, scoops, Frankensteins, sprint.
cue: Next group goes at the free-throw line
h: Add a sprint finish on the last trip.

st: Go to half court with the called movement

why: Wakes up hands and footwork with crisp, on-target passes.
say: Face your partner, step into every pass, and catch with ready hands.
how: Partners stand 12–15 feet apart.
30 seconds each: chest, bounce, overhead, one-hand push.
Step toward your partner on every pass.
h: Non-dominant hand only, or add a shuffle between passes.

st: Step and pass to your partner
Return it — switch pass type every 30 seconds

why: Grooves a clean shooting motion before range shooting.
say: Start close, shoot with one hand, hold your follow-through until it lands.
how: Start 3 feet from the rim, one hand under the ball.
Make 5, take one step back.
Work out to the free-throw line, then add the guide hand.
cue: Wrist snaps — hand in the cookie jar
e: Use a lower rim or smaller ball.
h: Must swish 3 in a row to move back.

st: One-hand form shots close to the rim

why: Classic warm-up that gets everyone moving and finishing.
say: Shooting line attacks the rim, rebound line grabs it and passes to the next shooter.
how: Shooting line at the right elbow-extended; rebound line on the left wing.
Shooter dribbles in for a right-hand layup.
Rebounder grabs it, outlets to the next shooter.
Players switch lines after each rep.
cue: Hit the top corner of the box
Talk: call the next shooter's name
h: Switch to left side, left hand.

st: Dribble in from the right side
Right-hand layup off the glass; rebounder steps in
Rebounder grabs it, shooter goes to the rebound line
Rebounder brings it back to the shooting line

why: Team-building warm-up where coach can see everyone.
say: Circle up around center court and follow the leader's movement.
how: Team forms a circle around center court.
Coach or captain calls a movement: arm circles, leg swings, lunges, hip openers.
Jog a lap of the circle between moves.
h: Players lead and explain why each stretch matters.

why: Wakes up defensive stance and hips early.
say: Stay low and slide corner to corner without crossing your feet.
how: Lines start on the baseline corners.
Slide diagonally 3–4 steps, drop step, slide the other way.
Go to half court, jog back.
h: Go full court and sprint the last stretch.

st: Slide corner to corner, drop step at each turn

why: Everyone gets touches right away — no standing in lines.
say: Three stations, 2 minutes each: form shooting, ball handling, footwork. Rotate on my whistle.
how: Split into three groups.
Station 1: form shooting close to the rim. Station 2: stationary ball handling. Station 3: footwork around two cones.
Two minutes, whistle, rotate clockwise.
Coach floats and corrects one thing per player.
h: Add a fourth station: partner passing.

st: Shooting, ball handling, footwork — all at once

why: Warms up legs and hands together — dynamic moves while dribbling.
say: Keep the dribble alive while you do the move — high knees, skips, shuffles, backpedal.
how: Lines on the baseline, a ball each.
Go to half court with the called movement while dribbling.
Jog back down the sideline with the other hand.
Moves: high knees, skips, side shuffles, backpedal, lunge-and-dribble.
h: Add a crossover every three steps.

st: Move to half court while dribbling
Back down the sideline, other hand
